questions.q: What real problem does terraform import solve?
options: A resource that already exists but that Terraform has no record of, needing to be brought under management without recreating it
A resource that needs to be deleted and recreated from scratch
A .tf file that has a syntax error
A resource that only exists in a plan, never actually deployed
questions.explain: Import binds a real, already-running resource to Terraform's state without touching the resource itself.

questions.q: Does terraform import write the matching resource block in your .tf file for you?
options: No — you must write the resource block yourself, describing what you believe already exists
Yes, it always generates the full resource block automatically
No, because import does not require a resource block at all
Yes, but only for storage accounts
questions.explain: Import only binds an existing resource's ID to a block you've already written — it does not author that block for you.

questions.q: What does terraform import actually bind together?
options: The real Azure resource's ID and a resource address (like azurerm_storage_account.data) in state
Two separate Terraform state files into one
A Bicep template and a Terraform resource block
Two different Azure subscriptions
questions.explain: That binding is what makes Terraform consider the already-existing resource "managed" going forward.

questions.q: Why should you always run terraform plan immediately after an import?
options: Import doesn't check that your resource block matches reality field for field — a plan diff reveals any mismatch
Plan is required to actually complete the import process
Plan deletes the imported resource if something went wrong
It's not necessary — import guarantees a perfect match automatically
questions.explain: A plan with no changes confirms your block matches; any diff means the next apply would touch a resource that's already live.

questions.q: What real-world risk does terraform import specifically avoid, compared to just writing a resource block and running apply?
options: Terraform recreating (destroying and rebuilding) a resource that already exists and is in use
The resource costing more money in Azure
The resource being visible in the Azure Portal
The resource block containing any variables
questions.explain: Without import, Terraform would try to create a resource with the same name from scratch, risking a real production resource being destroyed and rebuilt.
